headline: Bulgaria Shields Journalists From Abusive Lawsuits
meta_description: Bulgaria passes landmark law defending journalists and activists from intimidation through abusive lawsuits, extending protections beyond EU requirements.
summary_short: Bulgaria's parliament has passed a law protecting journalists and activists from abusive lawsuits designed to silence critics—going further than required by Europe.
body:
Bulgaria's parliament passed a law this week aimed at protecting journalists, activists, and others from abusive lawsuits designed to censor or intimidate critics.

The reform implements a European directive from 2024, which requires EU member states to shield journalists from abusive cross-border lawsuits within the bloc. However, Bulgaria has chosen to extend these safeguards beyond what the directive mandates—the law also covers purely domestic cases. This voluntary expansion means critics and journalists face less risk of intimidation through litigation, whether the lawsuit originates across borders or within Bulgaria itself.

The move reflects growing concern across Europe about "strategic lawsuits against public participation"—cases filed not to win on merit, but to drain resources and silence speech. By protecting both cross-border and domestic cases, Bulgaria has signalled a commitment to free expression that reaches deeper than minimum EU standards require.
quick_facts: Bulgarian parliament passed journalist protection law this week
Law shields journalists from abusive lawsuits meant to intimidate critics
Implements EU directive from 2024 with voluntary domestic extensions
Covers both cross-border and purely domestic cases in Bulgaria
